astar-research-attachment-programme-arap.about:
The A*STAR Research Attachment Programme (ARAP) connects overseas universities with A*STAR, Singapore's lead public research agency. PhD (and postgraduate) students based at overseas universities spend 1–2 years in an A*STAR research institute working on a joint project under co-supervision by their home supervisor and an A*STAR researcher, in biomedical sciences, physical sciences, engineering, infocomm and related fields.

Students are nominated jointly by their home university and A*STAR supervisors. A*STAR researchers submit nominations by 1 June or 1 December each year, and attachments can start six months after the award. Applicants need at least a Second-Class Upper honours bachelor's degree (or equivalent), strong references and a good research record.

Awardees receive a monthly stipend and housing allowance, a one-time IT allowance, airfare grant and settling-in allowance, visa costs, medical insurance and a conference allowance.
highlights: Fully funded 1–2 year research stay in Singapore
Access to world-class A*STAR facilities
Two nomination rounds a year (1 June, 1 December)
astar-research-attachment-programme-arap.eligibility: Overseas-based PhD/postgraduate students with at least a Second-Class Upper bachelor's degree (or equivalent), strong referees and a research track record, nominated jointly by their home university supervisor and an A*STAR supervisor. Students at ARAP partner universities contact their university's ARAP office.
how_to_apply: Identify an A*STAR researcher whose work fits your PhD and discuss a joint project (with your home supervisor).
Check whether your university is on the ARAP partner list and contact its ARAP office.
The A*STAR supervisor submits the nomination by 1 December 2026 (or 1 June 2027).
If awarded, start the attachment about six months later.
astar-research-attachment-programme-arap.costs: Fully funded: monthly stipend, monthly housing allowance, IT allowance, airfare grant, settling-in allowance, visa cost, medical insurance and conference allowance.

cuhk-summer-institute-secondary-2027.about:
The CUHK Summer Institute (SI) is a two-week summer programme for secondary school students who will apply to university the following year. Students take one or two short academic courses from 20+ options taught by 40+ CUHK scholars, join orientation and enrichment activities, and experience campus life with 350+ local and international participants.

It is open to Grade 11 (American system), Year 12 (A-level), IB DP year 1, Gaokao Senior 2, Taiwanese Senior 2 and equivalent international curricula, aged 16+ at the start. Credits can count towards future undergraduate study at CUHK (terms apply).

Non-local students live on campus. Merit awards (for students recognised by gifted-education bodies or recommended by their school) halve the programme fee.
highlights: University courses taught by CUHK scholars
Credits towards future CUHK study
Merit awards cut the fee by half
cuhk-summer-institute-secondary-2027.eligibility: Secondary students applying to university in 2028 (e.g. Grade 11, A-level Year 12, IB DP1, or equivalent), aged 16+ when the programme starts. Any nationality.
how_to_apply: Choose one or two courses from the SI course list.
Create an account in the online application system (opens early March) and upload your last two school reports.
Apply for a merit award (school recommendation) by the early-bird deadline if eligible.
Pay the HK$150 application fee within two days; accept the offer and pay fees within four days of results.
cuhk-summer-institute-secondary-2027.costs: 2026 non-local: two courses HK$9,200 (early bird HK$8,740; merit award HK$4,600), accommodation HK$3,300, activities HK$1,600, visa HK$100–730, application fee HK$150. Flights extra.

cuhk-summer-undergraduate-research-progr.about:
SURP lets senior undergraduates from overseas (non-Chinese) universities spend eight weeks doing research under a CUHK faculty member, choosing from 160+ topics across science, engineering, medicine, business, social sciences and humanities. In 2026 it ran from 21 June to 15 August with about 180 students.

Participants register in a 3-credit course ('Independent Research on International Studies') and receive a transcript; they devote at least 20 hours a week to the project and join orientation, cultural activities and excursions. On-campus housing (shared rooms) is guaranteed.

You can apply as an exchange student (if nominated by a CUHK partner) or as a fee-paying student. In 2026 the online deadline was 13 February; up to 10 tuition waivers go to strong applicants, with priority for financial need.
highlights: 160+ research topics in every faculty
3 credits and a CUHK transcript
Up to 10 tuition waivers; guaranteed campus housing
cuhk-summer-undergraduate-research-progr.eligibility: Full-time senior undergraduates in good academic standing at an overseas, non-Chinese university. English proof required if your university does not teach in English. Admission is decided by CUHK host supervisors.
how_to_apply: Browse the SURP research project list and choose topics.
Prepare a recent academic recommendation letter, transcript, passport copy and (if needed) English proof.
Submit the online application by the February deadline (exchange students also need home-university endorsement).
Once admitted, pay fees and apply for a Hong Kong student visa (6–8 weeks).
cuhk-summer-undergraduate-research-progr.costs: 2026 fee-paying students: tuition HK$8,150 (~US$1,050; up to 10 waivers), administration fee HK$4,000, optional on-campus housing HK$8,800, visa HK$100–730, refundable deposits. Exchange students: tuition waived. Travel and meals extra.

kyoto-icems-summer-internship-2027.about:
The Institute for Integrated Cell-Material Sciences (iCeMS) at Kyoto University, home of Nobel laureate Susumu Kitagawa's porous-materials research, runs a five-week intensive summer internship for undergraduates enrolled at foreign universities. Interns conduct independent research in a host lab on topics integrating cell biology, chemistry, mathematics and materials science (with a special emphasis on self-assembly), take part in academic events and the iCeMS community, and finish with a final presentation. 2026 host faculty included Daishi Fujita, Aiko Fukazawa, Shuhei Furukawa, Mineko Kengaku, Susumu Kitagawa, Daniel Packwood, Easan Sivaniah, Jun Suzuki and Motonari Uesugi.

The programme is designed as a stepping stone for students who might pursue graduate study at Kyoto University in an iCeMS laboratory. In 2026 applications opened on 15 January and closed on 26 February; details on dates, support and documents are published in each year's application guidelines linked from the iCeMS internship page.
highlights: Research in labs of world-leading chemists and cell biologists
Five-week programme with final presentation
Pathway toward graduate study at Kyoto University
kyoto-icems-summer-internship-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students at universities outside Japan (any nationality) who will complete at least two more semesters of study after the programme and are interested in graduate school at Kyoto University in an iCeMS lab. Kyoto iUP and SJTU students apply through separate tracks.
how_to_apply: Check the iCeMS internship page and news for the 2027 announcement (expected January 2027)
Read the application guidelines and choose preferred host PIs
Submit the application before the deadline (26 February in 2026)
Arrange visa and travel if selected
kyoto-icems-summer-internship-2027.costs: Financial support and any costs are set out in the yearly application guidelines (not confirmed for 2027); assume travel and living costs may be partly self-funded.

nig-intern-2027.about:
NIG-INTERN is the summer research internship of Japan's National Institute of Genetics (NIG) and the SOKENDAI Genetics PhD programme in Mishima. Interns carry out an independent research project under a host principal investigator, receive training in research and scientific communication, visit labs to talk with PIs, join graduate lectures, journal clubs and seminars, and present at the NIG-INTERN Reports Symposium, receiving a certificate on completion.

Selection is extremely competitive (six students chosen from more than 1,240 applications for 2025). The 2026 internship ran 8 June – 17 July with applications 1 December 2025 – 5 January 2026. For 2026 NIG covered round-trip airfare up to JPY 200,000 and travel insurance, while interns paid guest-house accommodation (about JPY 70,000 for 39 nights) and living costs. Applicants of any nationality are welcome.
highlights: Independent project in a leading genetics institute
Airfare (up to JPY 200,000) and insurance covered
Strong pathway into the SOKENDAI/NIG PhD programme
nig-intern-2027.eligibility: Students of any country or nationality interested in the life sciences who are in their pre-final year at the time of application (3rd year of a 4-year bachelor's, 2nd year of a 3-year bachelor's, 4th of a 5-year, 5th of a 6-year programme, or 1st year of a 2-year master's). Non-pre-final-year and PhD students are not considered.
how_to_apply: Read the application guideline on the NIG-INTERN page when the 2027 call opens (expected 1 December 2026)
Submit the online application before noon JST on the deadline (5 January in 2026)
Only the online system is accepted; results are posted as applicant numbers
Selected interns arrange visas and travel for June
nig-intern-2027.costs: No programme fee. 2026 terms: NIG paid round-trip airfare up to JPY 200,000 and travel insurance; interns paid NIG Guest House accommodation (about JPY 70,000 for 39 nights), domestic travel and living expenses.

osaka-university-international-summer-pr.about:
The International Summer Program (ISP) of the Graduate School of Science at the University of Osaka is an intensive research internship for overseas students in the natural sciences. Each participant joins an assigned research group in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biological sciences, macromolecular science or earth and space science, works on a thematic project under a host professor, and gives an oral presentation of results at the end. The programme also includes social and cultural activities with Osaka students and a one-day excursion, and is a good preview of the school's English-taught graduate programmes.

The 2026 edition ran 16 July – 27 August, with applications from 8 December 2025 to 13 January 2026 and results from end of March. Tuition is JPY 57,600 (waived for nominated students from partner universities) and the bench fee is fully waived; a limited number of participants receive a scholarship of about JPY 50,000 or more.
highlights: Hands-on research in a University of Osaka science lab
English-language programme with final presentations and certificate
Bench fee waived; some scholarships
osaka-university-international-summer-pr.eligibility: Current bachelor's or master's students at a university outside Japan, any nationality, with strong interest in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biological sciences, macromolecular science or earth and space science. Must remain enrolled throughout the programme (students graduating or changing degree level during the programme are not eligible) and attend all orientation and final events.
how_to_apply: Check the ISP page for the 2027 call (expected early December 2026)
Choose three preferred research groups from the department lists
Apply online with the required PDF documents before the deadline (13 January in 2026); tick 'Yes' for the scholarship if needed
Results end of March – April; arrange visa and housing with the school's guidance
osaka-university-international-summer-pr.costs: Tuition JPY 57,600 (waived for nominated partner-university students); bench fee waived; dormitory JPY 20,000–100,000 per month; local transport JPY 5,000–10,000; insurance about JPY 1,500; excursion about JPY 5,000. Travel to Japan self-funded. Limited scholarships of about JPY 50,000+.

purdue-surf-2027.about:
Purdue Engineering's Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships (SURF) programme, run by the Engineering Undergraduate Research Office (EURO), offers a 10-week immersive research experience. Fellows join a faculty-led project on Purdue's West Lafayette or Indianapolis campus, mentored by faculty and graduate students, in areas spanning engineering, computing, materials, energy, biomedical engineering and the sciences. The programme adds professional-development sessions on research skills and graduate school, and ends with every fellow presenting at the SURF Symposium.

For 2027 the programme starts with a remote week (31 May – 4 June), followed by in-person research 7 June – 30 July 2027 and the symposium on 29 July. It is a paid fellowship (the EURO site lists a USD 6,500 summer stipend). Undergraduates enrolled at Purdue, other US institutions and international institutions are eligible; international applicants must apply by 15 December 2026.
highlights: Paid 10-week research with Purdue faculty
Open to undergraduates at international universities
Professional development and a final research symposium
purdue-surf-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students enrolled at Purdue, other US institutions or international institutions (all nationalities), with interest in engineering or science research. International applicants must meet the earlier 15 December 2026 deadline and handle US visa requirements.
how_to_apply: Browse SURF 2027 projects on the EURO website once the application opens (early November 2026)
Submit the online application ranking projects of interest, with transcript, statement and reference details
International applicants: submit by 15 December 2026
Accepted fellows complete the remote week from 31 May 2027 and move in on 5–6 June
purdue-surf-2027.costs: No fee. Paid fellowship (USD 6,500 summer stipend listed by Purdue EURO). Travel, visa and housing arrangements should be checked with the programme.

unist-visiting-research-student-program.about:
The Visiting Research Student (VRS) Program at UNIST in Ulsan is for students from outside South Korea who want to carry out research in one of UNIST's laboratories (energy, materials, chemistry, biomedical engineering, AI, semiconductors and more).

There is no fixed intake: you contact the laboratory you want to join, obtain permission from the professor in charge, and then apply at least 45 days before your desired start date. Accepted students obtain a D-2-5 research-student visa using UNIST's documents and proof of funds (bank statement or research stipend).

It suits undergraduate, master's and PhD students who already have a potential host professor, for example for a thesis project or summer research.
highlights: Year-round, flexible research stays
Work in labs at a top Korean science university
Good way to meet a future graduate supervisor
unist-visiting-research-student-program.eligibility: Students based outside South Korea who have secured permission from a UNIST professor to host them. Proof of funding (bank balance or stipend) is required for the visa.
how_to_apply: Find a UNIST lab that fits your interests and email the professor.
Once the professor agrees, apply to the International Affairs Team at least 45 days before your start date.
Receive UNIST documents and apply for a D-2-5 visa at your nearest Korean mission.
Arrange health insurance and housing (on-campus guest house or off-campus).
unist-visiting-research-student-program.costs: Costs depend on the host lab (some labs offer stipends); visa fees, travel, insurance and living costs are usually your own unless the lab funds them.

uoft-deep-summer-academy-2027.about:
The Da Vinci Engineering Enrichment Program (DEEP), run since 2003 by U of T Engineering's outreach office, brings high-school students with a strong aptitude for science and maths to the University of Toronto's St. George campus for week-long courses on topics usually taught in upper-year undergraduate or graduate engineering, such as AI, robotics, biomedical, chemical, civil and electrical engineering. Courses are taught by U of T master's and PhD students and run Monday–Friday, 9:30–15:30. More than 10,000 students have taken part.

In 2027 courses run in four one-week sessions between 5 and 30 July. Students apply once to be admitted, then register for up to four course weeks; a residence option on campus is available for each session (residence registration closes in mid-June). There are separate tracks for grades 9/10 and 11/12, and international students pay a higher weekly fee.
highlights: University-level engineering topics taught by U of T graduate students
Choose 1–4 one-week courses; residence available
Open to domestic and international high-school students
uoft-deep-summer-academy-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 9–12 in the 2026/27 school year who have completed at least one year of high school. Grade 9/10 track: Grade 9 maths and science completed by June 2027; Grade 11/12 track: Grade 11 maths and science (chemistry and physics) completed. International students may apply (international fee rate applies).
how_to_apply: Join the DEEP mailing list and watch for Round 1 (early-bird, winter 2027) or Round 2 (spring 2027)
Submit the joint DEEP/CREATE application and pay the application fee (CAD 50 Round 1 / 60 Round 2)
Once accepted, register for up to four week-long courses while places last
Optionally book on-campus residence before mid-June 2027
uoft-deep-summer-academy-2027.costs: 2026 course fees (2027 may differ): CAD 732 per week domestic, CAD 1,111 per week international; discounts for 4 or 6 weeks. Application fee CAD 50–60. Residence is extra. Cancellation refund minus a CAD 135 admin fee until 7 days before the session.

ustc-fusep-summer-research-2027.about:
The USTC Future Scientist Exchange Program (FuSEP) Summer Research, run by the International College of the University of Science and Technology of China in Hefei, selects strong international students to work for six weeks on research projects in top-tier USTC teams supervised by USTC professors. Participants write a report on their findings and also attend academic lectures, visit world-leading national laboratories, tour Chinese cultural sites and meet USTC student clubs. Project lists are published on the FuSEP website.

The 2026 programme ran 22 June – 30 July with a deadline of 22 March 2026. Tuition, registration fees and on-campus housing are waived; excellent students receive a USTC Fellowship including a travel grant and meal plan, and outstanding participants are prioritised for scholarships if they later apply for USTC degree programmes.
highlights: Research in leading USTC science and engineering teams
Tuition, fees and campus housing waived; fellowships for travel and meals
Visits to national laboratories and cultural sites
ustc-fusep-summer-research-2027.eligibility: Full-time undergraduates or graduate students at their home university (any nationality outside China's mainland), who will have completed at least two years of undergraduate study in the relevant field by the programme start, with an excellent academic record, passion for research and good English.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list on fusep.ustc.edu.cn when the 2027 call opens
Apply online with transcript, CV, statement and recommendation as requested
Deadline expected around late March 2027 (22 March in 2026)
Contact incoming@ustc.edu.cn with questions
ustc-fusep-summer-research-2027.costs: No tuition, registration or on-campus housing costs. USTC Fellowship for excellent students covers a travel grant and meal plan; others pay travel and food.
